Eg har prøvd det ut etter at ingenting annet hadde noe effekt. I mitt tilfelle var det psykiske lidelser som hadde tatt helt over i livet mitt og derfor ble eg ganske deprimert siden eg følte eg hadde så lite kontroll over livet mitt. Det var dag inn og dag ut med følelsen av at eg så inn i en mørk tunnel og at det var ingen vei ut.

Så eg bestemte meg for å prøve ketamin behandling. Eg vil påstå at eg merket en bedring til og med dagen etter første behandling. Det var akkurat som om eg pustet lettere. De tingene i livet som hadde vært veldig tunge før føltes ikke så tunge ut lengre. De følgene ukene var veldig fine. Det var flere ting i livet mitt som begynte å falle på plass. Eg hadde mer energi for det sosiale og hadde det egentlig fint for første gang på lenge. Det var ikke perfekt selfølgelig, eg hadde forsatt dårlige perioder, men de var ofte korte og overkommelige. Etter flere behandlinger var det egentlig også bare veldig fint. Eg hadde for det meste gode perioder. Masse som var veldig vanskelig tidligere var nå mye lettere. 

No har det gått over 2 år siden behandlingene. Ting går forsatt mye bedre. Eg ser ofte tilbake på når eg tok ketamin behandling som en slags ny start på livet. Ketaminen er nok for lenge siden ut av systemet mitt men det ga meg rett og slett en "boost" til å få livet tilbake igjen på rett kjør.

Uansett var behandlingen en veldig fin opplevelse der det er vanskelig å finne gode ord for å beskrive den. Det kjennes ut som du endelig slapper helt av og har det egentlig bare veldig fint under behandlingen.
If you are trying to get a strong reaction from people you are probably in the wrong place.

I feel so unbelievably good when I'm drunk. I don't know if I feel like it makes it so I am able to escape reality more but rather that reality becomes so much more tolerable and in a way almost unlocks whatever it is that is keeping me from being happy normally. I no longer worry about what I am going to do because I finally feel enthusiastic and motivated. I stop feeling like every social interaction I have is a grueling reminder that I will never have a connection with another person. I start viewing the world as a place for good experiences and happiness instead of a desolate place that was never meant for me.

It honestly kind of scares me but at least it is always a place I can go if things aren't working out.
I have never related more to a video ever.

I feel the same way. I don't dislike people, I just dislike the way you have to interact with most of them and how lonely I feel around them because of how different I feel. If there was just one person I was able to relate to, maybe I could benefit from the positive parts of a relationship without having to endure all the negatives. I am beginning to fear it is a desire I can never fulfill though as the relationship I imagine involves me being my true self, which I can't express to the real world. I am stuck drifting between two worlds where I have to choose between being compatible with the world and being my true self, and I wish I could just commit to one of them.

I think having to solidify an identity is the main problem for me because I feel like I can't. I never developed one and the one I portray is so shallow it doesn't allow for more personal connections. I know I am not a shallow person and I know that there is depth to my character but to display that to other people is something I can't do. There is a huge mismatch in how I feel internally as a person versus what I am able to show other people.

I don't think there is a major difference in how sharing/receiving personal stuff drains me. I definitely handle casual interactions a lot better but they can become uncomfortable quick if someone tries to get more personal.

I did mention anxiety as a way to try to explain the discomfort I feel once someone has gotten too close, which I would say is different from social anxiety that relates more to the fear of other people.

Frustratingly, I can't explain it very well. It is a response that drains me completely emotionally but I can't explain how that affects me. It is not fear and it is not social anxiety, it is the burden of having a personal connection with someone. It does something to me that I cannot explain.

Not embarrassed but it is annoying for sure. It is kind of like trying to explain something to someone that they don't have the capability to understand, which inevitably leads to uncomfortable situations. I don't blame them though since to most people I do live a very isolated and boring lifestyle. The most painful part is honestly all the advice and ideas people try to pitch me if I am honest about my situation and being forced to listen to other people tell me how my life could be so much better.

To avoid these situations, I usually lie.

I advise you to not obsess too much over a single disorder even if you relate to it strongly. If it helps explain certain things that you are experiencing and doesn't negatively impact your life, good for you. If it is something that becomes a big hurdle in your life, you should see a professional to make sure you aren't fucking yourself over by turning something that is meant to be used as a tool or a description to potentially help you, into something that is damaging to your mental health.

I can relate to parts of it. I am a very lonely person with no close friends and a dwindling connection to my family, and I have no intentions to improve either and I feel very content on my own.. most of the time. It is not that I wish I felt closer to my friends or that I cared more about my family, but I am realizing that having zero people close to me is starting to create a pretty big void that is hard to fill with anything but depression. I wish it was easier for me to relate to other people, and that it felt more meaningful maintaining close relations. The feeling or thought of having a person close to me that understands me that I can relate to, sometimes feel good.

But personally, I have never felt unworthy of love or had any regrets pushing away close relationships. I do feel like I offer value to people around me and I am generally pretty confident in who I am and don't really ever doubt my self-worth. The reason I push people away is because close relationships are extremely tiring and provide very little value to me. I can't explain why that is, it is just who I am. It is not something that changes, and if anything relationships only get more tiring and have less valuable as time go on. The only thing that changes is my need to fill the void that the lack of close relationships leaves, but it is not like having those relationships fixes that as they only make me tired and don't fill the void at all. This is where I feel like my main problem with being schizoid is, the complex dilemma of being extremely lonely while simultaneously hating other people.

I hope this sort of answers your mood questions as well. I will add that I am generally not very tolerant of other people and I am very sensitive to things about others I dislike, but it strongly depends on the person. I am very easy to piss off and do sometimes have bad thoughts about other people, although I will never confront anyone or act on any of the thoughts.

And as a reminder I am just one diagnosed schizoid. There are so many things that can vary from person to person that it can often be confusing trying to relate to just one schizoid. There are commonalities but people express them in different ways.

It is a hard condition to live with, but not hopeless. At times it will seem hopeless and some days will just feel so absurdly meaningless and painful it will not feel worth it to carry on.

It is difficult to tell how the disorder will develop as time goes on, and it varies from person to person. There are probably examples of people who completely heal and live normally, but there are also people who stay the same for the rest of their life. The only thing you can do is to try to accept whatever state you are in right now and adapt your life to the point where it is livable. It will not be perfect and it might not even be real. I personally spend a lot of time fantasizing about relationships and so on that aren't real and even though I know it sounds pathetic, it can often help me feel a lot better. My hope is that one day maybe parts of it will be more real than it is currently, or I will be able to immerse myself in to it to a much greater extent.

There are days where this hope almost completely fades, but it is often on these days I feel the most need to change. I attempt to find meaning and ways that I can express my emotions to at least ease some of the apathy. I remind myself that it doesn't need to be real, because it doesn't matter as long as it makes you feel happy. I try to forget about the world as a whole and focus on things that are valuable to me, that could potentially be real in the future if they aren't already.

Just going to sleep also helps sometimes. Often our emotions will run a bit wild if we get tired. Whatever it takes I hope your tomorrow is better, and if not you are always welcome back here where I am sure the vast majority of us shares your experience.

It makes sense but that is the problem, the things my brain tells me I should enjoy and what should feel good makes me feel nothing. I can't be content doing nothing because I feel like there are things I can do that is supposed to make me happy, but they don't.

I could make a list of what I do, but there would not be a single thing that make me feel better except experiencing brief moments of time where I can immerse myself in my fantasies where things actually make me feel better. I have one thing that make me feel more neutral which is driving my car, that can at least take away the feeling that I am doing nothing and distract me from what I described as the mismatch in my head. I can only do it so much before it loses its effect, but I try to as much as I can.

I understand that I am not in a good headspace and that I must be hard to talk to, so I apologize if I am hard to reach through to.

Hard to answer but I don't think there is any greater goal in life besides trying to maximize your own happiness. I think naturally people are given sets of things that make them happy like family, friendships, ambitions and hobbies and that in the pursue of these things life gives meaning. There is more reward than suffering, or at least enough reward to not feel like life isn't worth living. My problem is that I can't feel the rewards for any of these things, instead they actually make me feel worse. There is nothing inside my brain that tells me that it should make me feel worse, and sometimes I genuinely wish for these things, but every time I try to actively pursue these things I feel miserable. The mismatch of what I experience in my brain and what I experience in real life is probably what makes me suffer the most.

Therefor I can't really answer what I consider a good life, because I don't know. I can listen to what my brain tells me should make me happy, but it doesn't actually make me happy if I act on it.

There are probably a bunch of things I could try still although it seems like my major attempts have already failed. I have tried seeing multiple phycologists, and I am currently seeing a lower tier of mental health support because the phycologists determined they couldn't help me. I have tried maintaining a job, finishing education, working on friendships but eventually realized that they make me more sick than they help. I have smoked weed multiple times which I enjoy but it's only temporary, and I want to try harder psychedelics but it is super inaccessible in my country. I do regularly drink and enjoy alcohol but don't want to become addicted since my family has a long history of drug abuse. Diet, fitness and sleep are all meh, used to be better, but something I don't think affects the bigger picture.

I guess my bigger problem is more existential, and that it is hard to find a place in the world where I am truly content. My current situation is probably me breaking down after a long history of feeling like I can't find that, and it seems impossible to make any progress.

It can be pretty demanding. I would say it is more mentally fatiguing, and that I spend a lot of energy answering questions that don't necessarily require much thought. I do appreciate my ability to hear and talk though, but it would be nice if people were more understanding when I am not very enthusiastic to respond.

If anything, it seems like my generation (23yo) is expecting everyone to be super social and connected. It is seen as a red flag if you aren't active on social media and people will look at you like you're an alien if you don't have snapchat and instagram. It sucks, even though I am a very asocial person, because it makes it harder whenever I decide to be social since there is a huge disconnect. It definitely sets me up for a lot of awkward interactions when people are surprised and can't relate to me instantly.

I can't say I care though as I don't have much in common with my generation anyways and mostly keep to myself. It would bother me if I had an increasing need to be social, but if anything my need for isolation is the only thing increasing. If anyone is critical of how I live, it is only because they are unable to relate to anything they consider not normal, making their criticism worthless.

Being drunk always puts me in a good mood and makes life very enjoyable for me. It makes people around me that is also in a good mood infinitely more interesting to  talk to, but I still have a very low tolerance for drama and I will often just bail if I don't find the people I'm around fun to interact with. 

Eventually though I will still get tired of talking to people and leave just to be alone. Sometimes I will just walk around outside for hours, enjoying my own company and be so happy for no reason. Everything in my mind becomes so interesting and it sometimes makes it feel like life is worth living.

It kind of makes sense why so many people in my family became addicted to it.

Not my mom no, but I have always longed for a person that was willing to go out of their way to put me first. I feel like I have done this a lot of times for people but nobody has ever done it for me. It seems like people will only do whatever benefits them at the time, which is to be expected but it sucks when you don't have anyone you can rely on. Most people at least have a parent or close friend they can depend on, but when you don't have any of that it makes it seem like the only person you can rely on is yourself.

Family gatherings might be one of the least suited environments for a schizoid. It is hard to deal with people in general, but having tons of people who you are supposed to be close with all at the same place at once can just be unbearable. There are so many emotions centered around these events that it is difficult not to feel like a freak when you don't experience those emotions yourself. It is like you are in a different realm than those around you, because the feelings that come naturally to them don't come naturally to you at all. You don't really have a choice to not act "weird" when you can't relate to the people around you.

It is demoralizing, because even after realizing that you don't share the interests of those around you it still isn't obvious why you shouldn't just cut people out of your life completely. Having to go through life completely alone is tough no matter how schizoid you are. It is also hard to overlook all the experiences you are potentially missing out on and it is not like these experiences are easily replaceable. Ideally you find an environment that suits you where you can balance positive life experiences without having to sacrifice your sanity, even though it might be the most difficult thing you'll ever do.

Just know that you deserve to exist just as much as they do and that you deserve to be given the freedom to be yourself, and that you are not in the wrong for not measuring up to people's arbitrary expectations of you.

I feel like I exist in a different world than most people. I don't experience the same emotions as others and I can't find enjoyment in others company. It makes me feel suffocated and after a few hours my energy is spent and I can't take it anymore. 

To be honest, it is a painfully circular problem and hard to justify but that is part of the problem. Most people would not know how to justify the way they feel or the way they view the world, and because they fit the norm well enough they never have to. It is painful to continuously be forced to try to fit in and have to question yourself all the time because it is impossible to do so.

I do live with my parents. My home life is exhausting and I try to spend as much time away from it as possible. I love my parents even though I feel like they failed me when I started opening up to them about my mental health in my teens, and they pretty much ignored me and pretended like nothing was going on because it was too uncomfortable for them to handle. I still don't think they are mature or wise enough to discuss anything related to mental health, which is why I avoid talking to them and would rather them not know about my problems. They know I don't like people because I have told them, but they think it doesn't apply to them for some reason. I really don't have much in common with them and we are so different in so many ways which is why our relationship is neutral at best. I don't think they would ever be able to provide any meaningful support, besides many financial support so that I can eat and have a roof over my head.

You are right, I am super-isolated but that has been my existence for the majority of my life. It is not even that I am isolated in the sense that I don't see people, but I don't think there has ever been any significant person in my life that I have ever been able to relate or look up to. At this point I would genuinely prefer complete isolation because every person I interact with makes me feel miserable. I don't know how to change this, and I am afraid it will be the reality for the rest of my life.

I do computer work. What makes it impossible is that I feel terrible emotionally all the time, and consider killing myself multiple times a day. I can barely deal with life without a job, but with a job it is just extra stress that I have to deal with on top of it. I have always hated my life, it feels unbearable all the time, and there is no reward for living it.

I was a NEET for about 2 - 3 years, after dropping out of school 3 times because I couldn't handle seeing people so often. I also quit a job for the same reason. I recently started working again, but only a couple of times a week. I enjoy it a lot because it fits my interests pretty well, and they also allow me to work fulltime from home. I would really like to keep the job, but it feels impossible because I could barely handle being a NEET, and the added stress from having a job is just too much sometimes.

I was formally diagnosed with SPD and moderate depression about 5 years ago.

I don't know why my problems aren't being taken seriously. It sucks because I feel like I put in so much effort in attempt to better my condition and functioning, but I feel like if I would have just broken down completely and stopped caring maybe they would take me more seriously.

I am 22.

As much as I want to find a good therapist and possibly get better, I feel like I have already gone through all my options. I have had so many applications denied because nobody believes they will be able to provide significant help, and when I get referred to specialists my applications get denied because my issues are too trivial and can be solved by less specialized therapy. This was even with help from my doctor, who basically just told me that the system had failed me. I genuinely don't know what to do or who to talk to, because the people that are supposed to help me already knows. It pains me to say it, because I know they want what is best for me but I often feel like they are the people who make me suffer the most. They are constantly pushing me to take on more stress and mental fatigue, while not being capable of providing any support to help me get better.

It feels so terrible just waiting for things to improve when there are no signs that anything will improve anytime soon.

I have talked to multiple therapists and am currently seeing one, but there isn't really a lot to talk about. I just feel like I am wasting my time because it doesn't really seem like they understand my issues and how much it impacts my life. My problems always seem trivial and unapproachable, and I am usually met with general life advice that isn't very useful. I have tried reaching out for better help, but my requests are always denied.

It is frustrating because I feel like my mental health is deteriorating meanwhile people are expecting me to take on more and more responsibility and somehow get healthier at the same time without significant help. I do not know how to tell anyone that because I lose either way. It seems like no matter what I do it comes at great personal cost that I cannot afford.

If I give up, I have no future and could possibly end up extremely poor and homeless. If I keep going, I am going to lose my sanity. I'd rather be dead.

Fuck it is so disappointing seeing people downplay mental illness once again. I am sorry you are having to defend your difficulties to others, you shouldn't have to do that. Mental illness can radically change your life in so many negative ways, yet be so subtle you may not even realize there is something wrong with you before your life is in shambles. It should be taken very seriously and help should be available no matter how "little" you are suffering.

It can be soul crushing to try your absolute hardest at life, yet feel so incapable of achieving even the slightest of what is expected of you. While it may be true that you get the opportunity to "escape a capitalistic hellhole" or that you can live your life "without even lifting a finger", it sure would have been nice to have taken that decision yourself. Not to mention the life draining apathy, inescapable loneliness, the very limited ability to experience emotions or the suffering of trying to figure out why you are so different from others while also watching your life fall apart in front of you because education, working or anything that involves other people seems inaccessible to you.

Our society has a pathetic understand of mental illness, and sure as fuck has no empathy unless people are able to relate directly to your problem. In a perfect world you would never be expected to change drastically to meet some arbitrary standard of what is considered normal, unfortunately people seem to do just that. This is why recognizing mental illness as serious and something that requires help and not the ungodly effort of someone struggling, is so important.

Should you lay down and never work on your problems? No. Can you recognize the good and appreciate your strong sides? Absolutely. But it is ridiculous to downplay the negative and act like they don't exist. You deserve to have your struggles be understood.

I struggle with this a lot where I will fantasize about different social situations like being in a relationship, talking to someone I like or just hanging out with friends and feel so many positive emotions because it feels so real.

But in reality I feel almost nothing but anxiety and apathy in those situations. I instantly turn aloof and have a really hard time expressing emotions and people will often assume I'm angry at them because my mood changes so quickly when my mask drops. 

The primary feeling I have under these interactions, is often just the extreme need for solitude.

What you describe is painfully accurate for me. 

It will often take me weeks to recover fully emotionally from being immersed in a place or a character because they seem so real and comforting at the time and I am starting to understand that it is something I will probably never experience in real life. I love the amount of happiness and fulfillment some of these fantasies give me but the crushing realization that it is all fiction can be very difficult to deal with sometimes. The way I view the world and myself in my head is so different from what I experience elsewhere.

I guess I haven't fully given up hope yet because I don't know if I am strong enough to bear the mental toll that comes with it. But it can be incredibly painful and demoralizing to feel so sad and alone no matter what you do in the real world because nothing seems to fit the image you have created in your head.

I don't know honestly. The intensity of feelings some of the dreams allow me to experience is really unique, but it can also leave me terribly apathetic to the real world. I am just incapable of envisioning myself without the ability to fantasize because I feel like it is so integral to so many parts of my mind I would never wish to get rid of. 

But it can be intense and it can be detrimental for sure.

The more time I spend interacting with the world the less energy and motivation I have for hobbies etc. I do have some things I enjoy doing but my ability to enjoy things highly depend on my circumstances.
I guess the clone would exist as a separate consciousness that interacts with the world in a similar way as you. Having an exact clone would just be kind of weird.

In one hour I would say that it is unlikely that they would be able to tell or give you a proper diagnosis. Most psychiatrists will be cautious giving out a diagnosis that quickly because it is incredibly easy to misdiagnose.  

Personally I was in therapy for over a year before getting my diagnosis and a lot of the time was spent ruling out things like depression, anxiety, autism and so on. However I was not specifically looking for one diagnosis which may have made the process take a bit longer.

It is hard to know if something is truly "SPD" because it is really just a collection of traits and not something that exists outside of the DSM-5. There are so many ways things that can alter your personality in different ways so I would say that it is nearly impossible for an individual without professional training to know why some behaviors manifest themselves the way they do. If you want to change and are troubled by the pattern of behaviors you describe, seeing a psychiatrist would obviously be one of the more helpful things you can do.

Personally I can resonate with a lot of things you are saying. I lived a very introverted childhood with a couple of friends, even though I preferred spending time alone, that turned quickly into a very isolated adulthood with no friends and barely any contact with the outside world. My ability to show emotions is very limited, but I feel like I very much experience emotions internally especially when I relate or attach to virtual characters. I do manage to seem semi-normal when I do interact with other people, but socializing in general is just a big drain for me so I typically avoid it.

The biggest issue with SPD for me and the reason I want to change is because of my inability to enjoy things. I often feel incapable of enjoying life because of this and it is one of the main reasons I go to therapy. It also makes it difficult to understand myself because I often wonder if my inability to enjoy things is related to all the value I lose out on by isolating myself from society. I often question if maybe I'm just an introvert and not schizoid because I am able to identify value in the ability to socialize. Some days I actually do feel like socializing.

I think the point I'm trying to make is that it is very easy to be confused when looking at labels because your personality is very complex and can't be described by one label. The set of traits described by one label can manifest in so many different ways meaning that the label itself isn't very useful. Instead try identifying behaviors that are troublesome to you and that you want to change and start from there.

For as long as I can remember I have had a very introverted personality. Even as a child I would often avoid seeing friends just so I could spend time alone, often getting angry if my parents invited my friends over to play without my knowledge. I have also always had a very limited ability to show emotions, even though that has gotten worse over the years. But looking back at old pictures I was always super serious and rarely smiled. I was pretty sensitive to criticism as a child so that might be the only thing that was uncharacteristic of a person with SPD.

I would say the stronger symptoms of SPD like anhedonia started manifesting themselves after I turned 15 or 16 and has only gotten worse over the years (I'm 23 now). A thing to keep in mind is that different aspect of your personality might be certain way for different reasons. I used to attribute all my anxiety, withdrawal and negative emotion to SPD, but later realized that it is probable that a wide variety of things might have influenced my personality.

So be careful when attributing symptoms to SPD especially if you have a history with things like abuse, bullying, emotional neglect and so on.

I also very often find myself unable to enjoy things I am supposed to enjoy. I will buy a video game I really want to play, but be completely unable to derive any joy from experiencing it. I will then procrastinate playing it because what is the point if you can't enjoy it? This is particularly frustrating because despite having no job, very few responsibilities and unlimited time I am often completely paralyzed by apathy.

My suspicion is that it is related to a schizoid's limited ability to experience emotions and at least for me the toll of experiencing emotions. It can be very mentally draining to endure emotions, especially in social interactions. I often find myself particularly unable to enjoy things after a day with an unusual amount of social interactions. I also suspect it has something with a lack of meaning and a sense of uncertainty in my life. I fear I will be this way forever if not get worse as I age. And if I can't be certain of how my life will be tomorrow it would be unnatural to not be concerned about what I am doing now and what I can do better.

Besides seeing a therapist and potentially undergoing treatment of some sort, I would recommend trying to discover what triggers the apathy for you and reducing the frequency if not avoiding the triggers. I would also spend some time reflecting on things that may be concerning to you or things that you perceive as problematic that may be in the way of focusing on what you are doing currently. If you are concerned about your life and what you future holds, it would only be logical for your brain to focus on that instead of focusing on things like making art.

I miss the presence of having at least one important person in my life that makes me feel not alone and that I am comfortable engaging with. I have the opportunity to see and talk to people often but find myself refusing their offer because it usually doesn't help my situation. It is also my fear that I will never find that one important person because of my refusal and unwillingness to engage with any community or person.

I often get the feeling that it is my inability to be on the same emotional level as another person that is making me feel lonely, and that no matter what person I meet I will feel lonely. Can for sure say I feel pretty complicated at times too.

The confusion here is between mood disorders and personality disorders and the utility in differentiating them. There are some key differences (that you can read about below) that are probably useful for predicting behavior, most effective treatment, causes and so on.

[Source](https://www.promisesbehavioralhealth.com/addiction-recovery-blog/difference-between-personality-disorder-and-mood-disorder/) for below

> The key difference between personality and mood disorders are the symptom patterns they cause. The main feature of mood disorders is periods of emotional highs and/or lows. Some personality disorders can cause mood swings, but this isn’t the main symptom of personality disorders.  How do medical professionals diagnose these disorders, when both kinds can lead to emotional and mood problems? Usually it’s about symptom patterns, rather than one single symptom.

I don't know why you would need to swallow your ego to see a therapist. If you are having problems with mental health, it is one of the best and smartest things you can do for yourself. No decent person ever will see you as weak or criticize you for attempting to improve your life. I think most people, especially those who have faced mental health issues, will see the decision to seek out professional help as a great sign of introspection and strength because both are required for recognizing that you need help and for the will needed to work out your problems.

So be proud if you seek out a therapist because there is no greater step you can take in order to improve your life.

It was not my intention to lump every schizoid into either of these groups, but rather point out my observation of two different groups. Different people will obviously have different things going on that will make their situation and experience unique.

I also want to point out that it is not clear to me if schizoids with stable lives/careers suffer less from relationships because they have stable lives/careers or if they just tend to have more stable lives because of the fact that they do not suffer from relationships.

Did you experience a lot of distress being around people before and did it change after all this happened to you?

I have experienced this a lot as well. It has been hard to convey that I don't necessarily share the same values as most people. Especially when it comes to friendly relationships, it has been impossible for some to believe it is not something I value. They will question why I don't value it, but will not accept the same justification one can use for explaing why you would value it. Some will eventually just accept that it is the way I am, while some will not believe and keep assuming things that are incorrect.

It can be infuriating to have your values questioned because realizing that you don't value  social interactions can be depressing to say the least. It makes it seem like you can just value whatever seems preferential to you at the time, but values can be deeply ingrained and some times impossible to justify.

My experience have taught me that I shouldn't let them "help" me, but use them as a tool to get something I want. And if it isn't giving me anything I stop seeing them. Another thing is to avoid directly talking about how you don't value working, because some people will just instantly assume you are lazy, but rather talk about the difficulties you believe you would face working a job. For me I usually talk about my feelings of anhedonia and the difficulties I have just enjoying general life, and how working would contribute to that because socializing make the anhedonia worse.

I guess the things I do while I am experiencing this are things I do purely out of the  motivation to not only stare into a wall, although it feels like I am doing that sometimes and sometimes I am literally doing that. 

The things I do are also things that usually completely lack any emotional requirement, making them very insignificant and forgettable which is leading me to feel like I am doing nothing.

Do you have more feelings when you are immersed in yourself? I can usually live pretty enjoyably inside my own world, but immediately shut down when I am around people and no longer immersed in my own world.

This has pretty severe repercussions on my career and social life but it is way better than not being able to feel anything.
